item.title: Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery ahead of major South America trip in November
item.description: Addressing the public during his traditional Sunday noon blessing, Leo thanked those who had expressed concern and asked them to keep him in their prayers. The pope said the abnormality had been detected at an early stage and was localised, adding that he had decided to proceed with surgery on medical advice.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Colorado woman protects 18,484 acres of family ranch once listed for $100 million
item.description: A Colorado woman has permanently protected 18,484 acres of her family's cattle ranch, once listed for $100 million, from future development. Susan Nottingham's decision preserves land her parents spent over 60 years assembling, along with historic water rights linked to the Colorado River. The agreement also protects wildlife habitats while allowing the ranch to continue agricultural operations.

item.title: Nepal floods: Chilling videos show bridges swept away, homes destroyed
item.description: A sudden flash flood in Gorkha district along the Budhi Gandaki River has wreaked havoc, causing severe destruction and displacing many families. With reports of multiple homes and bridges lost, at least ten individuals are currently unaccounted for. In light of the crisis, authorities have deployed rescue teams and helicopters to aid in evacuations.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Australian developer sues for A$100 million after rail project stalls 218-apartment construction
item.description: An Australian property developer has sued Victoria's Suburban Rail Loop Authority for at least A$100 million after a railway project stalled construction of 218 apartments in Melbourne for two years. The dispute concerns the government's acquisition of underground land, leaving more than 100 homebuyers waiting for their apartments.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Houthis exempt Mecca, Medina airports from attacks as Riyadh vows revenge
item.description: On Sunday, the Houthis issued a warning against using Saudi airspace for all but Mecca and Medina airports. This warning follows an attack on Riyadh's international airport that resulted in civilian casualties and fatalities. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree indicated their targeting actions would continue based on a tit-for-tat strategy. Saudi Arabia vowed retaliation, labeling the attack a war crime and a violation of international law.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Poland holds emergency meeting over possible attack on PM Tusk, defence minister
item.description: Polish security services convened an emergency meeting following a reported threat against Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. Authorities have been on high alert due to recent violent incidents at schools in Poland. These incidents led to arrests and concerns about online glorification of violence among youth. Tusk emphasized the spontaneous nature of these acts, suggesting no organized group is involved.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: In 1958, voters rejected a $15 million reservoir; 68 years later, judge overturns Lake Ringgold permit
item.description: A recent ruling by a Texas judge has nullified the permit for Wichita Falls' proposed Lake Ringgold reservoir project, which sought to address acute water shortages caused by ongoing drought. This controversial plan raised red flags among ranchers and conservation advocates, as it would affect approximately 16,000 acres of land, threatening to uproot numerous ranching families. The city is now contemplating an appeal and strategizing alternative water solutions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Three Indians rescued from attacked cargo ship in Black sea depart for India
item.description: Amidst a distressing attack on the Turkish-owned MV Royad Mammadov cargo vessel in the Black Sea, three Indian nationals were successfully rescued. After receiving medical care in Romania, they were declared stable. The Indian embassy played a crucial role in ensuring their safe return and provided necessary supplies during their ordeal. Unfortunately, the attack also led to the loss of two foreign seafarers' lives, underscoring the gravity of maritime risks.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: A Vietnam War veteran turned discarded materials into Colorado's famous Cano's Castle
item.description: Cano's Castle, a roadside attraction in Antonito, Colorado, was built by Vietnam War veteran Dominic “Cano” Espinoza using discarded beer cans, hubcaps, screen doors and scrap metal. Construction reportedly began in 1980. More than four decades later, a fire in January 2022 destroyed the residential section of the property, although its two main towers survived.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2024, Glenn and Barbara Britt gave Dartmouth College $150 M, easing tuition costs for families
item.description: In 2024, Dartmouth College announced a scholarship bequest of more than $150 million from former Time Warner Cable CEO Glenn Britt and his wife, Barbara Britt. The gift raised the annual family income threshold for zero parent contribution from $65,000 to $125,000, benefiting around 350 families each year. It also expanded scholarship support at Dartmouth's Tuck School of Business.

item.title: This couple's $100 million gift made Yale School of Music tuition-free
item.description: A $100 million donation by Stephen and Denise Adams in 2005 made Yale School of Music tuition-free for admitted students. More than 20 years later, the school continues to offer full-tuition awards and fellowships. The couple, who initially donated anonymously, also supported improvements to the school's academic programmes and music facilities.

item.title: Nasa-backed spacecraft to inspect dead space objects, test future repair and debris removal tech
item.description: NASA has launched a washing-machine-sized spacecraft to inspect up to four inactive satellites and rocket bodies in low Earth orbit. The SSPICY mission, launched on October 1, will begin inspections in early 2027. Using autonomous navigation, sensors and electric propulsion, the spacecraft will test technologies that could eventually help repair satellites or remove orbital debris.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 1967, an Australian man built a house from discarded glass bottles; today, it is a mining museum
item.description: Built in 1967 by Tex Moeckel, the Bottle House in Lightning Ridge is constructed from discarded glass bottles. The structure has become a tourist attraction and a museum showcasing local opal-mining history and vintage bottles. Initially serving as part of a miner's camp, it reflects the area's long mining heritage. Visitors can explore various artefacts linked to opal mining and local history within the museum.

item.title: Wild horses and donkeys dig desert wells in Arizona, supplying water to 57 vertebrate species
item.description: Researchers studied wild horses and donkeys in the Sonoran Desert, which dig wells that attract diverse wildlife. The wells serve as critical water sources for various vertebrate species during dry periods. Observations indicated that these wells significantly increase water accessibility and create favorable conditions for cottonwood seedlings. The study highlights the animals' role as ecosystem engineers in changing their environment.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Washington Supreme Court irrigation case: Farmer contests $618,000 irrigation penalties
item.description: Ron Fodé, a dedicated farmer from Washington State, is fighting against hefty penalties threatening his agricultural livelihood due to irrigation practices. The conflict arose in 2017 over water rights for his crops, leading to the Department of Ecology rejecting his irrigation assistance applications. This has resulted in penalties totaling $618,000.
